title: 1969 AHSME Problem 35
statement: Let \(L(m)\) be the \(x\)-coordinate of the left endpoint of the intersection of the graphs of \(y=x^2-6\) and \(y=m,\) where \(-6\lt m\lt6.\) Let \(r=\frac{[L(-m)-L(m)]}{m}.\) Then, as \(m\) is made arbitrarily close to zero, the value of \(r\) is:

solutions.text:
The left intersection satisfies \[ L(m)=-\sqrt{6+m}. \] Hence \[ \begin{aligned} r&=\frac{-\sqrt{6-m}+\sqrt{6+m}}{m}\\ &=\frac{2}{\sqrt{6+m}+\sqrt{6-m}}. \end{aligned} \] As \(m\) approaches \(0,\) this approaches \(\frac{2}{2\sqrt6}=\frac{1}{\sqrt6}.\)

Therefore, the correct answer is B.
hints: Substitute into \(r\) and rationalize the numerator
